hints.title: Prefix state
hints.body: Imagine consuming the candidate from left to right. At any point, some prefix of the first thread and some prefix of the second thread have been used. The lengths of those prefixes determine how much of the candidate has been consumed.

hints.title: Two-dimensional table
hints.body: Let `possible[i][j]` indicate whether the first `i` characters of `first` and the first `j` characters of `second` can weave the first `i + j` characters of `woven`.

hints.title: Look at the last character
hints.body: The current candidate prefix ends with either the last used character of `first` or the last used character of `second`. Try each source that matches and consult the state without that source character.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
if length(woven) != length(first) + length(second): return false
previous = row for consuming only second
for i from 1 to length(first):
    current[0] = previous[0] and first[i-1] == woven[i-1]
    for j from 1 to length(second):
        current[j] =
            (previous[j] and first[i-1] == woven[i+j-1]) or
            (current[j-1] and second[j-1] == woven[i+j-1])
    previous = current
return previous[length(second)]
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
